extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Expository textbook material (definitions, theorems, examples, and exercises) on projective geometry, gluing schemes, the Curve-to-Projective extension theorem, and the relationship between line bundles and Weil divisors. Includes constructions, necessary hypotheses, and illustrative counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product of base-point-free invertible sheaves is base-point-free
rubrics_metrics.description: If L and M are both base-point-free invertible sheaves on a scheme X, then L \otimes M is also base-point-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret via the Segre embedding: if φ_L : X → P^N and φ_M : X → P^M are morphisms coming from base-point-free linear series, the Segre embedding yields a morphism X → P^{(M+1)(N+1)-1} corresponding to the base-point-free series of sections of L ⊗ M. (See Exercise 16.1.B and Definition 15.2.1.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Segre embedding gives closed embedding for OPm(1)⊠OPn(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete linear series corresponding to OPm ⊠ OPn (i.e., O(1,1) on P^m × P^n) is base-point-free and gives the Segre embedding P^m × P^n → P^{mn+m+n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously checked by hand in earlier section (10.6.1) and can be deduced by Exercise 15.2.H; valid over any base Z. Use box-times notation F ⊠ G := π_X^* F ⊗ π_Y^* G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonexistence of nonconstant maps from projective space to smaller-dimensional quasi-projective varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasiprojective k-scheme X and a morphism π : P^n_k → X, either the image of π has dimension n or π contracts P^n_k to a point; there are no nonconstant maps from projective space to a smaller-dimensional quasi-projective variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: reduce to algebraically closed infinite k, write π^* O_{P^n}(1) ≅ O_C(d) and show d=0 by intersecting sufficiently many hypersurfaces using Exercise 12.3.C(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: GL_n action on projective space and stabilizer description
rubrics_metrics.description: GL_n acts (nontrivially) on P^{n-1}; over an algebraically closed field k the action is transitive on closed points and the stabilizer of [1,0,...,0] is the subgroup of matrices with zeros in the first column below the first row (parabolic subgroup P), suggesting P^{n-1} ≈ GL_n/P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Easier described functorially (see §15.2.3 and Exercise 7.6.S(a)); making the quotient precise requires defining group quotients in schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of a proper nonprojective variety by gluing
rubrics_metrics.description: One can glue two projective varieties along isomorphic closed subschemes to produce a proper scheme X that need not be projective; an example gluing two copies of P^3 along suitable P^1's yields a proper nonprojective k-variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show nonprojectivity, assume an embedding by L exists and compare restrictions of L to components and glued subschemes to obtain contradictory relations on degrees (e.g., n1 = 2 n2 and 2 n1 = n2). See Exercise 15.2.13 and Figure 15.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing schemes along isomorphic closed subschemes (construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given closed embeddings Z1 ↪ X1 and Z2 ↪ X2 and an isomorphism φ : Z1 → Z2, one can form the glued locally ringed space X1 ⊔_{φ} X2 by identifying the underlying sets along Z1 ≅ Z2, declaring opens to be those whose restrictions are open, and defining stalks as compatible pairs of germs agreeing along Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stalks at points not in the glued locus are the usual stalks; at points of the image of Z define O_{X,p} as pairs (s1,s2) in O_{X1,p} × O_{X2,p} that agree in O_{Z,p}. Exercises 15.2.O–15.2.Q guide making this a scheme (reduce to affine charts and the fibered product of rings construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of glued schemes with respect to categorical properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The glued scheme X1 ⊔_{φ} X2 is a fibered coproduct in schemes/locally ringed spaces and 'commutes with' flat base change; however, certain gluings (e.g., gluing X to itself along disjoint closed subschemes) may not produce a scheme but only an algebraic space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction preserves properties like properness/separatedness/finite type under suitable hypotheses on X1, X2 (see Exercise 15.2.R); but be aware of pathologies and category-theoretic subtleties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing preserves universal closedness, separatedness, finite type under hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If X1 and X2 are universally closed (resp. separated, finite type over a Noetherian ring A), then the glued scheme X1 ⊔_{φ} X2 is respectively universally closed (resp. separated, finite type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to the affine motivating example Spec(A1 ×_{A1/I1} A2) and uses Noetherianness to choose generators and show the resulting ring is finitely generated. See Exercise 15.2.R for constructive hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curve-to-Projective Extension Theorem (15.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose C is a pure dimension 1 Noetherian scheme over an affine base S = Spec A, p a regular closed point, and Y a projective S-scheme. Then any morphism C \ {p} → Y (of S-schemes) extends uniquely to all of C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness follows from reduced-to-separated arguments; proof reduces to Y = P^n and uses the 'clear denominators' idea: represent map by a line bundle and n+1 sections on C\{p}, trivialize on an open and clear denominators using a uniformizer t to obtain regular sections on C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary hypotheses for Curve-to-Projective extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The hypotheses (projectivity of Y, one-dimensionality and nonsingularity of C at the point p) are necessary: counterexamples show failure if Y is only affine, if C has higher dimension, or if p is a singular point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercise 15.3.A which gives explicit counterexamples: maps that can't be extended when hypotheses are violated (e.g., C = A^2, or C singular like y^2 = x^3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Central idea of proof — clearing denominators
rubrics_metrics.description: To extend a rational map C\{p} → P^n, represent it by n+1 rational functions f_i with no common zeros away from p, pick N = min val_p f_i and multiply by t^{-N} (uniformizer t at p) to get regular functions on C determining the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the effective translation of the 'line bundle with sections' description into coordinate functions; choose local trivialization and adjust by powers of a uniformizer to remove poles at p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension over regular codimension-1 points
rubrics_metrics.description: Rational maps from Noetherian k-schemes to projective k-schemes can be extended over regular codimension-1 sets: the domain of definition includes a dense open subset of a codimension-1 irreducible subvariety whose local ring is a DVR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercise 15.3.C and remark relating to the valuative criterion for properness; applies to extending over discrete valuation rings/generic points of divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Weil divisor
rubrics_metrics.description: A Weil divisor on a Noetherian scheme X is a formal Z-linear combination of codimension-1 irreducible closed subsets: D = ∑ n_Y [Y] with integers n_Y, all but finitely many zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weil divisors form an abelian group Weil(X). For curves this recovers divisors as finite sums of closed points. An irreducible divisor is [Y]; effective means all coefficients ≥ 0; support Supp D is the union of Y with n_Y ≠ 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisor of a rational section of an invertible sheaf (div(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is regular in codimension 1 and L is an invertible sheaf with a rational section s not vanishing identically on any component, then div(s) := ∑ val_Y(s) [Y], summing over irreducible divisors Y; val_Y(s) is defined via any local trivialization at the generic point of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The valuation is well-defined because different trivializations differ by units; val_Y(s) ≠ 0 for only finitely many Y. This generalizes zeros and poles for rational functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group of line bundles with rational sections and the div homomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Pairs (L,s) where L is a line bundle and s a rational section (not identically zero on components), up to isomorphism, form an abelian group under tensor product; multiplication by an invertible function gives (L,s) ≅ (L, t s). There is a group homomorphism div : {(L,s)}/iso → Weil(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identity is (O_X,1); the inverse corresponds to dualizing the line bundle and section appropriately. This map is the key bridge between line bundles and Weil divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of div on normal Noetherian schemes (Proposition 15.4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is normal and Noetherian then div: {(L,s)}/iso → Weil(X) is injective: if div(L,s)=0 then s has no poles and is regular globally, inducing an isomorphism L ≅ O_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: use local trivializations; zero divisor implies s is everywhere regular and invertible on trivializing opens, hence a global nowhere-vanishing section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of O_X(D) for a Weil divisor D
rubrics_metrics.description: For normal irreducible X, define O_X(D) by Γ(U, O_X(D)) := { t ∈ K(X)× : div|_U(t) + D|_U ≥ 0 } ∪ {0}; these are rational functions whose divisors plus D are effective on U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: sections are rational functions with zeros/poles constrained by D (positive coefficient allows a pole, negative demands a zero). Away from Supp D, O_X(D) ≅ O_X (Algebraic Hartogs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical rational section of O_X(D)
rubrics_metrics.description: OX(D) comes with a canonical nonzero rational section corresponding to 1 ∈ K(X)× (a section over the dense open complement of Supp D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This canonical section is used to relate O_X(D) to pairs (L,s) and to define div maps back and forth (see Exercise 15.4.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: OX(div s) ≅ L for a line bundle L with rational section s
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is invertible and s a nonzero rational section, then O_X(div s) is canonically isomorphic to L, via the map sending a rational function t to t·s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 15.4.F gives the construction and verifies that the canonical section 1 of O_X(div s) maps to s; normality is used to ensure the local domains form a basis of opens where the construction works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal and locally principal divisors and their relation to O_X(D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If D is principal (D = div(f)) then O_X(D) ≅ O_X. If D is locally principal then O_X(D) is an invertible sheaf. Conversely, if O_X(D) is invertible then D is locally principal (Exercise 15.4.I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus principal divisors map to the identity in Pic and locally principal divisors correspond to line bundles; caution about terminology: 'locally principal' used in two related senses in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example of Weil divisor not locally principal (cone example)
rubrics_metrics.description: On X = Spec k[x,y,z]/(xy − z^2), the line D defined by z=x=0 is a Weil divisor that is not locally principal, so O_X(D) is not invertible; however 2D is locally principal (div(x) = 2D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stalk at origin and tangent-space arguments to detect non-principality; demonstrates that multiplicity can make a divisor locally principal even if the underlying reduced divisor is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: UFD ⇒ O_X(D) invertible and Pic ≅ Cl (Proposition 15.4.15 / 15.4.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is Noetherian and factorial (UFD) then every Weil divisor D has O_X(D) invertible, so Pic X → Cl X is an isomorphism and Cl X ≅ Pic X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the affine case Spec A with A a UFD, Cl(Spec A)=0 and Pic(Spec A)=0; use local UFD property to produce local generators of codimension-1 primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic properties of the class group Cl(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cl(X) := Weil(X)/Prin(X) is the divisor class group; div : {(L,s)}/iso → Weil(X) descends modulo principal divisors to give an inclusion Pic X ↪ Cl X, with LocPrin/Prin mapping to classes of line bundles (diagram (15.4.10.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exact diagram relates line bundles, divisors, principal and locally principal divisors; it is central for computing Picard groups in normal Noetherian situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of removing closed subsets on class group
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing a closed subset of codimension >1 does not change the class group (doesn't change Weil divisors or principal divisors); removing an irreducible codimension-1 subset Z gives an exact sequence  Z ·[Z] → Cl X → Cl(X − Z) → 0 (excising a divisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for computations: e.g., Pic(P^n − Y) computations in later exercises rely on such excision sequences (see (15.4.11.1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Picard group of projective space and hyperplane class
rubrics_metrics.description: For X = P^n_k, Weil divisors correspond to homogeneous irreducible polynomials and Pic(P^n_k) ≅ Z generated by O(1) (the hyperplane class); deg O(d) := d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 15.4.H and 15.4.G show O(m) are all line bundles on P^n and Pic ≅ Z. Use restriction to subschemes to detect nontrivial bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twisting line bundles by divisors and section interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: For an invertible sheaf L and Weil divisor D on normal Noetherian X, define L(D) := O_X(D) ⊗ L. Sections of L(D) can be interpreted as rational sections of L whose zeros and poles are constrained by D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: (O(D1))(D2) ≅ O(D1 + D2); exercise 15.4.L(a),(b) gives precise descriptions and checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picard group of complement of a hypersurface (torsion example)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y ⊂ P^n_k is an irreducible hypersurface of degree d > 1, then Pic(P^n_k − Y) ≅ Z/(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercise 15.4.M; use excision exact sequence (15.4.11.1) and properties of hyperplane class to compute torsion in Pic of complements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Cartier divisors may restrict to non-principal elements in class group
rubrics_metrics.description: On U = P^n − Y (Y a hypersurface), the restricted hyperplane H_i gives an effective Cartier divisor on U that is not cut out by a single global equation on U, hence represents a nontrivial element of Cl(U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 15.4.O hints: otherwise it would be trivial in the class group. This shows Cartier-effectiveness doesn't imply principal globally on open complements.
